body.statement: Every \(\mathcal M\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ord}}\) has a value-equivalent canonical image in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{can}}\): push \(\nu\) forward by \(u\mapsto f^u\), so \(\mu(f)=\nu(\{u:f^u=f\})\). This preserves every factual and intervention-world evaluation, every explicit unnested score, and the observational law. Conversely, every \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{can}}\) is a member of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ord}}\) by taking \(\operatorname{pa}_i=\{1,\ldots,i-1\}\), \(\mathcal U=\mathfrak F\) with law \(\mu\), and \(\varphi_i(x_{<i},f)=f_i(x_{<i})\). Therefore, for every supplied \(p\) and score \(g\), the attainable set of \(\theta_g\) over observationally compatible models is identical in the two classes, and sharp-bound optimization may be carried out over the saturated carrier. This is the canonicalization and equivalence established by Rossetto--Antonucci for causal orders, restated as the compiler interface rather than as a novelty claim.
body.justification: The sourced equivalence licenses the compiler's saturated response carrier while keeping the target class equal to standard order-compatible recursive models with parent subsets.
body.gap: Rossetto--Antonucci supply this equivalence; it is an imported interface fact and carries no novelty claim.
body.consumer: The endpoint theorems can optimize over complete-predecessor response rows without redefining an arbitrary recursive structural causal model as saturated.
